content.overview: Article 14 of the Constitution of India forbids the State from denying equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. Classification must rest on an intelligible differentia that bears a rational relation to the object sought.
content.study:
Article 14 has two limbs: equality before the law and equal protection of the laws. Modern review also asks whether State action is arbitrary. Classification is permitted. Class legislation is not. After Maneka, Article 14 also informs the fairness of procedure under Article 21.

Practice: identify the class, the differentia, the object of the law, and the nexus. Then ask whether the measure is arbitrary in operation.

sections.heading: Text
sections.body: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Do not plead Article 14 as a slogan. Plead the class, the object, and why the differentia fails or why the action is arbitrary.
